executive_assessment.text: The new material differentiates Huye and Gisagara's reported vulnerability and adoption constraints from flood-exposed Volcanoes Region districts; these are selected examples, not a nationwide local ranking.

Gicumbi's adaptation fund reports training and funding reach, while the completion review could not establish use or effectiveness of the weather-information system. Outputs and intentions are not demonstrated resilience gains.

geographic_notes.text: Tearfund reports that Huye's vulnerability index declined to 0.556 over the previous five years as adaptive capacity strengthened, while Gisagara's index rose to 0.626.
Smallholder farmers were willing to adopt agroforestry and terracing, but limited training, quality inputs, and finance impeded uptake.

The review found national climate strategies relevant to local communities and associated with positive changes, but identified coordination and targeted-support gaps affecting the most vulnerable communities.
Tearfund described capacity-building for locally led restoration, especially with women, to strengthen community participation in environmental decisions and local monitoring and management skills.

The completion report identifies Burera, Nyabihu, Rubavu and Musanze in the Volcanoes Region as highly climate-vulnerable; it associates major floods with landslides, erosion, crop losses and infrastructure damage.

The 2022-2023 Gicumbi Community Adaptation Fund pilot supported 2,324 people, including 47.7 percent women, in 25 cooperatives with training and funding; 192 more people in 64 cooperatives received business-planning training.
The framework cites 74 percent of district roads as landslide-exposed and lists flood- and landslide-damaged road and bridge sites in 20 districts across all four provinces after the May 2023 rains.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification. Routine/default app-use approval does not certify claims or sources. 18 of 19 evidence records and 0 of 0 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
Opened sources report climate-related disaster losses and mobility but do not establish a country-specific climate-to-violence causal pathway.

The bank contains no completed mediated climate-FCV pathway; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.

No Rwanda-specific source found in the targeted search established an observed climate-to-FCV pathway; the only explicit country-specific link identified was a broad potential-risk sentence in a draft project ESMF.
The reverse-FCV search did not locate evidence that conflict, insecurity, or displacement has constrained Rwanda's climate adaptation or resilience delivery.
The UCLouvain full-text PDF and Tearfund full report could not be retrieved; their claims rely on accessible publisher abstracts and summaries.
The UCLouvain abstract does not identify the individual higher-risk cells, limiting finer subnational mapping.
Most resilience evidence covers plans, project outputs, or a pilot rather than independently measured reductions in climate vulnerability.
No new documented conflict mechanism was imported. The ESMF's generic border-conflict warning is retained only in the research audit, not operational evidence.
New district examples deepen selected local vulnerabilities and project outputs, not a complete national district risk ranking.
